A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BioX-Bridge work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-modal transfer experiments on ISRUC, FOG, and WESAD, including benchmark comparisons and architecture, position, and backbone ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds layer-selection diagnostics, further sensitivity analyses, a fully connected bridge comparison, and a reshuffled-subject experiment.

M1.justification: The two-stage probe/CKA selection, low-rank prototype bridge, alignment objective, and inference procedure are retained. The corrected CKA maximization agrees with v1's Figure 3 and 'most similar' description. Clarified initialization and probe notation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ISRUC sleep/wake, FOG detection, and WESAD affect/stress tasks across EEG, ECG, EMG, and PPG. Added analyses use existing datasets and transfer directions; reshuffling subjects changes the split rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Table A8 newly evaluates FC-Bridge, a fully connected bridge comparator. Table A9 also includes an ECG supervised oracle in the PPG-to-ECG comparison, whereas v1's corresponding Table A3b includes only the PPG oracle. Original benchmark comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include selecting bridge positions with 50% of WESAD data, additional parameter and training-fraction sweeps on ISRUC/FOG, and a reshuffled WESAD subject split using the original hyperparameters. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, performance metrics, and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D.4–D.8 substantially expand analysis: layerwise probing/CKA diagnostics, selection stability with reduced data, individual fixed-position heatmaps, ISRUC/FOG parameter and data-size sensitivity, an FC-Bridge architecture control, and subject-split robustness. The WESAD heatmap supplies a breakdown of the already reported fixed-position experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4 newly reports the coefficient of variation of CKA scores across layers, adding descriptive dispersion reporting. Existing five-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged. Revised standard deviations in Table A4 do not establish additional runs or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the backbone ablations retain their results. Tables 2/A4 revise fixed-position BAcc/F1-M/F1-W from 50.53/51.70/63.96 to 48.34/46.83/58.37, with revised deviations. Substantial additions include FC-Bridge's 48.59% balanced accuracy, BioX-Bridge's 54.13% on the reshuffled split, layerwise results, and a sharp FOG decline at 20% training data. The reshuffled result is not a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Equation 5 is corrected from minimizing to maximizing CKA. Equation 4 distinguishes the linear probe from the old modality's task head, and the pseudolabel expression now includes that task head. These repair the mathematical specification of the existing procedure; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same model-bridging contribution, two-stage selection and prototype architecture, and approximately 88–99% trainable-parameter reduction with comparable or better transfer performance. Added evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving final-layer error propagation, CNN versus transformer layer representations, relative versus absolute CKA similarity, input/output position importance, and teacher-dependent subject-split performance. Appendix B also adds the task-specific versus task-agnostic tradeoff and identifies multi-dataset and broader multimodal generalization as future work.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the supplementary-materials/future-repository statement with an explicit code repository address. Section 3.4 specifies random selection of training-set tokens or feature maps to initialize learnable prototypes. These improve documentation; the stated hardware, optimization settings, and original preprocessing instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B and its references add Zhang et al. (2022b), Liu et al. (2023), and Fang et al. (2024) to contextualize future multimodal and cross-dataset extensions. The existing positioning against distillation, translation, stitching, and domain adaptation is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory edits, clarifies oracle comparisons, improves appendix cross-references, adds acknowledgements, and updates the publication header. Additional appendix subsections organize the new analyses, while the main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix gains Figures A2–A10 and Tables A8–A9, substantially expanding visual presentation through layerwise curves, position heatmaps, sensitivity panels, and new comparison tables. Existing figures and tables are largely retained and reflowed rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The added architecture control, broader sensitivity analyses, and subject-reshuffle evaluation strengthen empirical support, while mathematical corrections and clearer implementation documentation improve reproducibility. Reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Figure A4 marks WESAD input/output layers 8/12, but Figure A8's caption states 7/8; Appendix D.8 also quotes 54.14% where Table A9 reports 54.13%.
